text: curious, when you just changed the whole compile step, did that potentially affect the physics of items, because i can now walk through some props and trees but i also had another worker working on physics already, i just want to make sure your change didnt silently affect the system so i can put it back on them
resolution: User asked whether my compile-step change could have silently broken prop/tree physics (they can now walk through some), since another worker is concurrently editing physics. Verified it cannot: my diff is 6 files, all transport + one console.warn log line (worldGeometry.ts) — zero collider/physics/footprint logic. The gamefile's COLLIDERS + PHYSICS_CONFIG lumps are produced by worldColliders.ts/createHmscMapfile/writeGameFile, none of which I touched; my code only runs after file=writeGameFile(...) and writes that exact Uint8Array to disk. Old base64-on-stdout and new raw binary write are both lossless, so for identical bake input the installed gamefile is byte-identical, colliders included. The real cause: my re-bake (run to test the fix) regenerated the gamefile from the current working tree, which has another worker's UNCOMMITTED edits to exactly the collider/footprint sources — game/kinds/props.ts, game/physics.ts, state/hostPhysics.ts, game/build/catalog.ts, render3d/props/DataProp.tsx, plus new untracked imported-props files. worldColliders.ts bakes colliders from those, so their in-progress work got baked in. Walk-through-props is theirs surfaced by the re-bake, not my transport change — safe to hand back. Flagged that my compile fix remains uncommitted in the shared tree, so commits must stage by explicit path.
